nodes.title: The durable substrate — runtime (with_operation_run, fencing, atomic claim, reconcile, sandbox lifecycle)
nodes.intent: Realizes §5.1-5.5 crash-durability without a broker via three Postgres primitives: with_operation_run heartbeats a running row (and bump_activity keeps the sandbox alive during silent work); the heartbeat IS the fence (rowcount 0 => reclaimed => is_owner=False, self-terminate, every emit verb gates on is_owner so a zombie can't double-speak); the atomic claim (INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING id, created_by=instance-id) is the sole cross-process coordinator; run_reconcile_sweep + the three-guard sandbox lifecycle (E2B timeout + explicit destroy + TTL reconcile, no ManagedResource FSM, no warm pool) prevent leaks; recycled orchestrator reloads meeting_cost, never resets to 0.

NOT done if any emit verb bypasses is_owner, a broker/in-memory cross-process lock appears, or cost resets to 0 on recycle.

nodes.title: Per-tenant envelope-key crypto isolation + crypto-shred offboarding
nodes.intent: Realizes the §4 per-tenant encryption floor and §15 offboarding invariant: a KMS-encrypted PD is the floor, plus a per-tenant envelope key over each tenant's subdirectory (a single shared key across tenants is the named anti-pattern), so offboarding = destroy the key = crypto-shred bounded to that tenant; run_reconcile_sweep() extends to delete a tenant's Postgres rows + GCS prefixes; a cross-tenant read is refused server-side; /internal/notes is token-gated outside the auth wall and resolves meeting_id->tenant so no meeting_id crosses into another tenant's notes.

NOT done if a shared tenant key exists, a shred affects another tenant, or a cross-tenant read leaks any row.

nodes.title: Ordered fail-fast boot lifespan + provisioner_ready + EPIPE tolerance + parallel shutdown
nodes.intent: Realizes §6 'fail loud at boot, not on first use': pydantic-settings validates the full required-key set at import (missing key => startup crash naming it); the ordered lifespan is init tracing -> open asyncpg pool -> construct Database facade -> provisioner_ready async gate -> boot-time stale-row reaper -> mount routers last (so a join can't race an unwired provisioner and no request sees a stale-running row); EPIPE from a crashed SDK subprocess is swallowed+recovered while unknown exceptions crash after a flush; shutdown gathers flush_tracing/db.close/bot.leave_all/server.shutdown in parallel with a backstop; the §5.7 sign-in/binding flow (users row + signed session cookie + resolve_session; meetings row bound to tenant/repo/pinned_sha + recall_bot_id round-trip) is wired.

nodes.title: Coverage read + Readiness gate — emits contracts.Readiness

The dropped span is recorded as an explicit comprehension gap on the transcript plane, never silently missing. The applier is a single writer per meeting: `add` mints a stable kind-prefixed id (c14/d3/a5), `patch` updates by id keeping the prior value superseded-not-erased — this patch-in-place is why the object grows with content, not time. The delta append AND the window's transcript_segments 'pending'→'comprehended' flip happen in ONE Postgres transaction (the replay-idempotency linchpin): crash mid-apply leaves the window 'pending' for exactly-once reprocessing; ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING is belt-and-suspenders.

nodes.title: Rolling-summary generator — cadence-refreshed Segment B, off the hot path, byte-stable between refreshes

nodes.title: Dual storage plane — Postgres append-only ledger (uuid, ON CONFLICT) + boot-reaping + GCS versioned artifact
spec_refs: 03-MEETING-UNDERSTANDING.md#3.3 (boot-time stale-row reaping, JOIN operation_runs, §11.2 uuid cast)
nodes.intent: Realizes §3.3's dual storage plane, split by write model. Plane 1 (Postgres, append-only, status-tracked): transcript_segments + note_deltas append every few seconds (GCS whole-object writes would thrash), asyncpg over the Cloud SQL Auth-Proxy socket, thin repos no ORM. The live in-memory NOTES_CACHE object every downstream consumer reads is the deterministic left-fold of note_deltas in id order — single-writer per meeting, so a reader sees a consistent snapshot and a crashed harness rebuilds by replaying the ledger (this live plane is load-bearing for Doc 04's Tier-3 session recovery — J-09-S5). Plane 2 (GCS, native Object Versioning + optimistic concurrency): the polished markdown notes file is a whole-object write with if_generation_match — None=unconditional, 0=create-only, <gen>=exact prior — turning the close-summarizer-vs-human-edit race into a 412 caught as NotesGenerationConflictError; generations are uint64, NEVER coerced through float.

nodes.title: The one dispatch funnel — rate-limit → registry-lookup → validate → meeting/entity isolation → route
nodes.intent: The single coroutine every inbound WS channel_action flows through, replacing the current 3-line stub dispatch() (which only checks is_owner and echoes the payload). It runs the ordered funnel of §4.3: (1) rate-limit per-connection via the pinned `limits`/`slowapi` in-memory backend (not a hand-rolled bucket, §11.11); (2) registry lookup by declared type; (3) Pydantic-validate once centrally (§4.2); (4) meeting/tenant isolation keyed on meeting_id PRESENCE — a handler never sees an un-isolated message, and the default-reject floor refuses a scoped message with no meeting_id; (5) entity→owner→tenant resolved from OUR store (never the client's meeting_id) killing the smuggle-a-foreign-id bug; (6) route to the exactly-one handler. Every failure returns a generic 'Not found'/'Slow down.' — never a type/tenancy leak. Auth is guaranteed at the connection upgrade (gateway), never per-message. This funnel IS the isolation guarantee that makes an unchecked route structurally impossible.

NOT done if isolation is opt-in per handler, if any error message distinguishes absent-vs-foreign-tenant, if the client meeting_id is trusted to authorize an entity, or if the rate limiter is hand-rolled.

nodes.integration_point: tests/e2e/test_s4_barge_in.py driving barge-in / quiet / stop against the live speak + abort path
nodes.acceptance: WHEN a human speech onset occurs during Proxy speech THE SYSTEM SHALL stop TTS within 200ms and flush; WHEN 'stop' is issued THE SYSTEM SHALL abort the in-flight build finally (no resurrection) and a human ask SHALL preempt.

abort-is-final (a killed build is never resurrected)
barge-in stop <200ms with small-chunk Output-Media buffer

resume/JSON-retry resurrecting an aborted build violates abort-is-final

nodes.title: S5 — hours-long meeting survives an instance recycle
nodes.intent: Prove S5 across 04·03·00: kill the orchestrator mid-meeting; a replacement re-claims the meeting on the operation_runs atomic-claim index (the claim frees only after the reconcile reap), replays recent transcript from Doc-03's transcript plane, and continues seamlessly; meeting_cost reloads from its persisted row (budget NOT reset to 0). This proves the two-tier durability + heartbeat/atomic-claim/reconcile substrate holds under a Cloud Run recycle.
nodes.definition_of_done: After a mid-meeting kill, a fresh harness re-claims via the atomic claim (post-reap), replays transcript_segments, resumes the meeting, and check_meeting_budget reads the reloaded (non-zero) meeting_cost. Not done if the meeting double-claims, loses transcript context, or resets cost to 0.
nodes.integration_point: tests/e2e/test_s5_recycle.py killing the orchestrator mid-meeting and asserting re-claim + replay + cost reload
nodes.acceptance: WHEN the orchestrator is killed mid-meeting THE SYSTEM SHALL let a replacement re-claim after reap, replay recent transcript, continue, AND reload meeting_cost (budget not reset to 0).
invariants: atomic single-claim on operation_runs (no double-claim)
budget survives recycle (meeting_cost reloads, not reset)
two-tier durability (session resume → transcript replay)
risks: claim frees before reap → two harnesses run the same meeting (split-brain)
cost reset to 0 on reload silently un-caps the budget

nodes.title: S6 — concurrency: several meetings on one host, no cross-meeting starvation
nodes.intent: Prove S6 across 04·05: several meetings run on one host at once with no cross-meeting starvation (per-meeting harness + per-host in-flight bound), each meeting's tenant isolation holds (the isolation triad — per-tenant volume+process+index, one tenant never sharing with another), and E2B sandboxes are provisioned/reaped independently per meeting. This proves the spine scales to concurrent meetings without one starving or leaking into another.
nodes.definition_of_done: N concurrent meetings each make progress (no starvation under the per-host in-flight bound), a cross-tenant read tripwire never fires, and each meeting's sandbox is provisioned and reaped independently. Not done if one meeting starves another, a sandbox leaks across meetings, or the isolation triad is violated.
nodes.integration_point: tests/e2e/test_s6_concurrency.py running concurrent meetings on one host and asserting fairness + isolation
nodes.acceptance: WHEN several meetings run concurrently on one host THE SYSTEM SHALL keep each making progress with no cross-meeting starvation, hold each tenant's isolation, and provision/reap each sandbox independently.
invariants: isolation triad (per-tenant volume+process+index, never shared)
cross-tenant read tripwire (runtime)
per-host in-flight bound (no starvation)

the in-flight bound starving a low-priority meeting instead of fair-sharing

nodes.title: S7 — cost circuit-breaker: soft-cap degrade with disclosure, hard-cap notes-only
nodes.intent: Prove S7 across 03·04·05: a meeting with real builds crosses the two-meter envelope (CANONICAL §12.7: listening baseline vs metered task budget). check_meeting_budget reads model_usd+transport_usd+e2b_usd; the soft cap (0.8×) degrades gracefully — Orchestrator→Haiku, Scribe interval widened — WITH a spoken disclosure; the hard cap (1.0×) goes notes-only. Never a silent cliff. This proves cost is an honest, disclosed SLA, not a hidden kill.
nodes.definition_of_done: Driving spend past the soft cap downgrades the Orchestrator model + widens Scribe with an audible spoken disclosure; past the hard cap it goes notes-only; every transition is disclosed (no silent degradation). Not done if degradation happens silently, the wrong meter trips it, or the hard cap kills the meeting outright instead of notes-only.
nodes.integration_point: tests/e2e/test_s7_cost_breaker.py driving spend across the soft/hard caps
nodes.acceptance: WHEN meeting spend crosses the soft cap THE SYSTEM SHALL degrade (Haiku + wider Scribe) with a spoken disclosure; WHEN it crosses the hard cap THE SYSTEM SHALL go notes-only — never a silent cliff.
invariants: never a silent cost cliff (every degradation is disclosed)
two-meter model (listening baseline vs task budget, §12.7)
never-overstate (Law 2: honest disclosure of degraded mode)
risks: degradation not spoken aloud = silent cliff
using the false all-in $1 instead of the two-meter sum trips the breaker wrong

nodes.title: S8 — honest failure: says what it can't see, never confident-wrong
nodes.intent: Prove S8 across 01·05·02: when the index is not-ready (with gaps), a tool errors, or there's an STT gap, Proxy says what it can't see and never gives a confident wrong answer (Law 1, grounded-or-silent). A failed Workroom build returns needs_review/failed via the fail-closed verify gate — never 'done'. This proves honesty under partial information: the readiness not_ready+gaps signal, the never-throw tool boundary, and fail-closed verification all route to an honest voice.
nodes.definition_of_done: With codeintel returning not_ready+gaps (or a tool error, or STT gap), the answer is an honest 'I can't see X' with the coverage gap named — never a fabricated answer; a failed build returns needs_review/failed, never 'done'. Not done if any of these produces a confident wrong answer or a failed build reports success.
nodes.integration_point: tests/e2e/test_s8_honest_failure.py driving not-ready / tool-error / STT-gap / failed-build paths
nodes.acceptance: WHEN the index is not-ready, a tool errors, or STT drops THE SYSTEM SHALL say what it cannot see (never a confident wrong answer) AND a failed build SHALL return needs_review/failed, never done.
invariants: grounded-or-silent (Law 1: say 'not found by this method', never confident-wrong)
tool handlers return errors never throw (never-throw boundary)
fail-closed verify (failed build → needs_review/failed, never done)
risks: a tool that throws instead of returning an error crashes the turn instead of degrading honestly
a build that times out reported as 'done' instead of failed

nodes.title: S9 — tenant isolation: message without a valid owned meeting_id is rejected
nodes.intent: Prove S9 across 08 (the dispatch funnel): a meeting guest opening the public connect page or sending a crafted tile message without a valid OWNED meeting_id is rejected. The single http.dispatch funnel enforces rate-limit → Pydantic-validate → meeting/tenant isolation keyed on meeting_id presence → entity→owner→tenant server-side resolution → handler. No cross-tenant read of customer code ever occurs. This is the isolation invariant at the inbound edge (negative/adversarial path).
nodes.definition_of_done: A crafted inbound message lacking a valid owned meeting_id (or with a foreign meeting_id) is rejected at the dispatch funnel before any handler, and no cross-tenant code read occurs (tripwire silent = clean). Not done if a foreign meeting_id resolves to another tenant's data or a message without meeting_id reaches a handler unmarked-global.
nodes.integration_point: tests/e2e/test_s9_tenant_isolation.py sending crafted/guest messages at the dispatch funnel
nodes.acceptance: WHEN an inbound message carries no valid owned meeting_id (or a foreign one) THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it at the dispatch funnel with no cross-tenant code read.
invariants: isolation (one tenant never reads another's code; cross-tenant read tripwire)
lethal-trifecta: untrusted inbound is data, never authority
meeting_id-presence isolation at the single dispatch funnel
risks: a global-marked message path used as a bypass
entity→owner→tenant resolution trusting a client-supplied tenant id

nodes.title: Demo arc — one continuous run spanning ALL docs
nodes.intent: Prove §4: ONE continuous run spanning all docs — connect a real repo → reach ready with a coverage % → invited to a meeting → answer two grounded questions (one via grep/read direct-answer, one via get_dependents) → asked to draft an impact summary → does it in the Workroom, verifies it, leaves a needs_review draft card → the orchestrator recycles once (chaos test) and continues seamlessly → cost stays in-envelope → meeting ends → notes file + staged draft persist → a human accepts the draft after the call and it applies. Every law observed, every claim cited, every world-touching act gated. This is the whole-product 'comes together' proof — the composition of S1+S2+S3+S5+S7 in one narrative.
nodes.definition_of_done: A single continuous e2e run passes the full arc: ready+coverage, two grounded cited answers, a verified needs_review Workroom draft, one mid-run orchestrator recycle with seamless continuation, in-envelope cost, persisted notes + draft, and a post-call human accept that applies (draft.accepted + notes.finalized). nodes.acceptance: WHEN the full demo arc is run as one continuous session THE SYSTEM SHALL connect→ready→answer two grounded questions→produce a verified needs_review draft→survive one recycle→stay in cost envelope→persist notes+draft→apply a post-call human accept, with every law observed.

never-overstate (Law 2)
human control is absolute (Law 3)
dynamic-not-hard-coded (Law 4)
talk-and-glance (Law 5)
budget survives recycle
lethal-trifecta containment

the recycle mid-arc losing draft/notes/cost context
